title: 3D buildings: soft edges, ambient occlusion, real facade lighting, roof shapes

labels.name: roadmap
labels.description: Planned work, shown on the website roadmap page

body: Our 3D buildings read as flat, pasted-on blocks with hard 90° edges next to Mapbox GL JS's. Close the gap: contact ambient occlusion on the ground, bevelled edges, a per-fragment material with a real facade gradient, and OSM building parts / roof shapes instead of one flat extrusion per footprint. ## The gap, item by item Caveat: our reference shot is a grey style at flat ambient, theirs is a dusk style with a strong directional light. Part of the difference is configuration, not code — A/B at the same sun hour before charging it all to the renderer. What is genuinely missing: | Gap | Mapbox property | Ours today | |---|---|---| | Contact darkening on the ground around each footprint | `fill-extrusion-ambient-occlusion-ground-radius` (3 m), `-ground-attenuation` (0.69) | **nothing** — buildings sit on an unmodified ground, which is why they read as pasted on | | Soft / bevelled vertical and roof edges | `fill-extrusion-edge-radius`, `fill-extrusion-rounded-roof` (default `true`) | hard 90°; `tesselatePolygon3D` emits raw walls | | Facade gradient over the whole wall | `fill-extrusion-vertical-gradient` (default `true`), `-ambient-occlusion-radius` | exists, but as `1 - 0.65/(1+h²)` in **absolute metres**, evaluated **per vertex** — dead above ~2 m, so a tall facade is flat | | Lit windows / emissive at night | `fill-extrusion-emissive-strength` | none | | Wall-vs-roof tonal separation | their 3D lighting mode | one Lambert term; roofs fall back to **view-direction** lighting on the legacy path | | Complex buildings — parts, roof shapes | `building` layer parts | one extrusion per footprint, flat roof | | Stipple artifact on tall walls | — | shadow acne. A bug, not a missing feature | ## Plan **Track 0 — renderer refactor** (~2-3 d, own PR, zero behaviour change) — shared with #131: - `begin3DPass()` / `end3DPass()` extracted from `renderGeometry3D`, the per-covered-tile walk extracted from `renderShadowCasters`, and `renderTileGeometry` split into common uniform setup vs vertex-layout binding. - One `applyLighting3D(color, normal, normalizedHeight, sideVertex, ao, emissive)` contract that extrusions **and** 3D models call, so a model and the wall beside it agree under the same sun. - Done when: A/B screenshot at a building camera is pixel-identical. **A4 — shadow acne on walls** (~1-2 d). A bug and the cheapest item, so it goes first. Isolate before touching any constant; the caster-offset reasoning is in [08-lighting-sky-fog.md](https://github.com/massif-maps/MassifMaps/blob/master/docs/internals/rendering/08-lighting-sky-fog.md). **A1 — per-fragment material** (~2-3 d). A normalized wall-height varying (0 at base → 1 at roof), an AO term over a radius in metres, a roof-edge term, emissive. New `Polygon3DStyle` fields plus CartoCSS `building-vertical-gradient`, `building-ao-intensity`, `building-ao-radius`, `building-emissive-strength`. Defaults reproduce the current look, so no app changes on upgrade. **A2 — edge radius / rounded roof** (~3-4 d). The "less sharp sides". Geometry work in `tesselatePolygon3D`: inset roof ring plus a bevel band, with shader displacement along an edge-distance attribute. Roughly +30 % roof vertices. Biggest single visual delta of the set. **A3 — ground ambient occlusion** (~3-5 d). Design decision to make first: bake it into the per-tile **drape** texture (orthographic, footprints already known, free at draw time) or add a ground-effect draw in the 3D pass. The drape is cheaper and fits our architecture; mapbox uses a scene pass because they have no drape. 3D models get contact darkening from whichever we pick — without it a model floats exactly the way our buildings do now. **A5 — building parts and roof shapes** (~5-8 d). OSM `building:part` features with their own base/height, and generated roof geometry (gabled, hipped, pyramidal, domed) from OSM roof tags. Partly a tile-data question — the parts have to survive into the vector tiles — and partly tesselator work. Scope to be split once A1-A3 have landed. ## Order and budget Track 0 → A4 → A1 → A2 → A3 → A5. Roughly **17-25 dev days**; all estimates, nothing measured. Each of A1, A2, A3 lands as one measured PR with a [performance-log](https://github.com/massif-maps/MassifMaps/blob/master/docs/internals/performance-log.md) entry at the city camera: per-fragment lighting, +30 % roof vertices and a ground-AO pass all cost fill, and city is already the tight camera (27 fps after the last perf round). ## Notes - **mapbox-gl-js v3 is licensed under the Mapbox TOS, not BSD.** Architecture and property semantics are a reference; no code or shaders are copied. tangram-ng, our usual reference, has none of these effects. - New style properties default to the current behaviour, so upgrading an app changes nothing until it opts in. - Documentation ships in the same commits, mostly in [08-lighting-sky-fog.md](https://github.com/massif-maps/MassifMaps/blob/master/docs/internals/rendering/08-lighting-sky-fog.md) and [11-tangram-diff.md](https://github.com/massif-maps/MassifMaps/blob/master/docs/internals/rendering/11-tangram-diff.md), plus a `docs/features/` page for the new CartoCSS properties. ## Related - #131 — 3D models from a data source. Shares Track 0, the lighting contract, and the ground AO from A3.

title: 3D models: draw GLB meshes from a data source, styled in CartoCSS

labels.name: roadmap
labels.description: Planned work, shown on the website roadmap page

body:
Place glTF/GLB 3D models from any data source — a GeoJSON file, an MVT layer — and style them in CartoCSS, the way markers and buildings already are. Many instances per tile, lit, fogged and shadowed by the same 3D scene as the extrusions next to them.

![Mapbox GL JS: 3D models placed from a GeoJSON source](https://docs.mapbox.com/mapbox-gl-js/assets/ideal-img/add-3d-models-using-geojson-source.2832262.960.png)

*Target: [Mapbox GL JS — add 3D models using a GeoJSON source](https://docs.mapbox.com/mapbox-gl-js/example/add-3d-models-using-geojson-source/). Image © Mapbox, hotlinked from their docs — replace with our own screenshot once we render this.*

## Why the tile path, not a vector element

The SDK already draws models: `NMLModel` + `NMLModelStyle`, drawn per element by `BillboardRenderer::drawNMLBatch`. That path has no CartoCSS, no tile streaming, no terrain drape, and does not participate in the shadow-caster pass.

Going through the tile path instead — a `model` symbolizer, fed by `GeoJSONVectorTileDataSource` like any other layer — buys all of it for free: per-feature expressions for rotation/scale/colour, tile culling, GPU draping on the terrain, fog, and shadows.

## What already exists

| Piece | Where | State |
|---|---|---|
| Mesh + material + texture GL drawing | `libs-massif/nml/` (`GLModel`, `GLSubmesh`, `GLMaterial`, `GLTexture`) | ships today, ES2, phong/lambert |
| Point-symbolizer → tile content, asset resolved by name | `MarkersSymbolizer` + `vt::BitmapManager` + `VTBitmapLoader` | the template for `ModelSymbolizer` / `ModelManager` |
| CartoCSS → symbolizer plumbing | `CartoCSSMapnikTranslator` (`building` is the closest analogue) | works |
| Shadow caster pass, cascades, receiver PCF | `GLTileRenderer::renderShadowCasters` | tile layers only — models hook into the same walk |
| GPU drape (vertex z from the elevation texture) | `GLTileRendererShaders.h` | model anchors drape the same way, with no CPU re-bake |
| 3D pass: overlay FBO, terrain-occluder depth seed, extrusion depth slack | `GLTileRenderer::renderGeometry3D` | models must draw **inside** it or they will not occlude buildings correctly |

Missing entirely: any glTF/GLB parser, any mesh geometry type in `vt`, instancing.

## Plan

Assumes the **OpenGL ES 3.0 baseline** ([graphics API migration](https://github.com/massif-maps/MassifMaps/blob/master/docs/internals/rendering/16-graphics-api-migration.md), Phase 2) has landed — instancing then is core, so there is one draw path and no ES2 fallback. UWP's `EGLContextWrapper` hardcodes client version 2 and must be flipped, or models silently do not run there.

**Phase 0 — renderer refactor** (~2-3 d, own PR, zero behaviour change; shared with the buildings work)

- `begin3DPass()` / `end3DPass()` extracted from `renderGeometry3D`: overlay-vs-inline decision, terrain-occluder depth seeding, extrusion depth-bias regime, composite.
- Extract the per-covered-tile walk from `renderShadowCasters` so a second caster kind hooks in.
- Split `renderTileGeometry` into common uniform setup (terrain / lighting / shadow / fog / blend) and vertex-layout binding, removing the `type != POLYGON3D` branch thicket.
- One `applyLighting3D(...)` contract that extrusions **and** models call, so a model and the wall beside it agree under the same sun.
- Done when: A/B screenshot at a building camera is pixel-identical.

**Phase 1 — GLB loader** (~3-5 d)

- `vt::Model`: plain struct — meshes (interleaved pos/normal/uv, `uint32` indices), materials (baseColor factor + texture, alphaMode, doubleSided), node transforms pre-flattened, bbox. Not `nml::Model`: that is protobuf, in another module, with a different material model.
- `vt::ModelManager` + `ModelLoader` interface in `vt`; `VTModelLoader` in `all/native` does the fetching (AssetPackage / HTTP / file), parses with **cgltf (MIT)** vendored into `libs-external`, decodes PNG/JPEG with the existing decoders. `vt` gains no new dependency.
- Scope: static meshes, baseColor + texture. No skinning, animation, Draco, KTX2 or meshopt in this phase — first task is checking whether the reference assets need any of them.
- Done when: `tower.glb` and `wind_turbine_static.glb` load on device and one instance is visible through the existing `NMLModel` path — no new render code yet.

**Phase 2 — CartoCSS + tiles + instanced draw + shadows** (~8-10 d)

- `ModelSymbolizer` in mapnikvt + translator entries: `model-file`, `model-scale`, `model-rotation`, `model-translate`, `model-color`, `model-opacity`. All expressions, so per-feature rotation/scale from GeoJSON properties is free.
- `ModelStyle` in `vt/Styles.h`; `TileLayer` gains `TileModelInstances` (model ref + packed instance array + feature ids) — a sibling of `TileGeometry`, not a new geometry type, since instances are not triangles.
- Instance record, 32 B: `vec4 posScale` (tile-local x, y, z offset, uniform scale) + `vec4 rot` (quaternion as normalized shorts) + `vec4 color` (RGBA8), divisor 1. One `glDrawElementsInstanced` per (tile, model, material), inside Phase 0's 3D pass.
- Terrain: the instance anchor is draped **in the vertex shader** from the elevation texture. Deliberate divergence from mapbox, who bake DEM z on the CPU and re-bake when exaggeration changes.
- Shadows: a `modelshadow` caster program reusing the instance attributes; receiving comes free from the existing `shadowReceiverFlags()` program factory, as do fog and the app's custom 3D lighting shader.
- Done when: a GeoJSON source plus a CartoCSS `model` rule puts N models on 3D terrain at a stated camera; they occlude and are occluded by buildings, cast shadows on the ground and on each other, and fog correctly.

**Phase 3 — scale and polish** (~4-6 d)

- Density reduction on mapbox's model (per-tile lookup grid, coarser at low zoom, off at z18+), opt-out.
- Far/near cutoff opacity fades; LOD (a GLB per zoom band).
- Picking: ray vs instance OBB.
- Transparent materials: back-to-front sort, two-pass when opacity < 1.
- Bench entry in [performance-log](https://github.com/massif-maps/MassifMaps/blob/master/docs/internals/performance-log.md): fps vs instance count at the city camera, on an Adreno 610.

## Cost and risks

Roughly **17-24 dev days** for the four phases, on top of the ES3 baseline. All estimates, nothing measured.

- Binary size: cgltf + the model renderer, estimated +150-250 KB per ABI, **unmeasured**. Should sit behind a `sdk_profiles.json` profile so apps that do not want models do not pay.
- PBR → our phong lighting is a downgrade; output will not match a mapbox screenshot exactly.
- Texture memory across many distinct models needs an LRU in `ModelManager`.
- **mapbox-gl-js v3 is licensed under the Mapbox TOS, not BSD.** It is an architecture reference only — no code, no shaders copied. Permissive references: cgltf (MIT), Cesium (Apache-2). tangram-ng, our usual reference, has no model support at all.

## Related

Documentation lands in the same commits: a new `docs/internals/rendering/17-models.md`, entries in both rendering index tables, a `docs/features/` page for the CartoCSS properties, and doc comments in `all/modules/*.i`.

- #132 — 3D buildings look upgrade. Shares Phase 0, the `applyLighting3D` contract, and the ground AO that keeps a model from floating.
